title: Motor Overload
cause: The motor is drawing too much current, likely due to a heavy batch or stiff dough.
fix:
1. Turn the mixer OFF.
2. Reduce the batch size.
3. Wait 2 minutes for the motor to cool.
4. Restart on a lower speed.

title: Drive Motor Overload
cause: Severe overload or stalled agitator.
fix:
1. Unplug the mixer.
2. Remove the obstruction (dough hook stuck?).
3. Allow 5 minutes to cool.
4. Plug in and restart.

title: Communication Error
cause: Loss of communication between the mixer controls and the motor drive.
fix:
1. Unplug the unit for 30 seconds to reset the VFD.
2. Check the interlock guard wire.
3. If it persists, replace the Control Board.

title: SC Pump Error
cause: The Steam Generator (SC) pump is defective or clogged with scale.
fix:
1. Run the 'CareControl' cleaning cycle.
2. Check if the pump impeller is blocked by debris.
3. Measure voltage to the pump (230V).
4. Replace the SC pump.

title: Gas Valve Error
cause: The gas valve is not opening or the ignition box is failing.
fix:
1. Check gas supply pressure.
2. Reset the unit.
3. Check the ignition electrode for sparks.
4. Replace the gas valve if no click is heard.

title: CleanJet Pump Failure
cause: The cleaning pump is not pumping water/chemical properly.
fix:
1. Check water pressure.
2. Ensure the cleaning tab drawer is closed properly.
3. Check for kinks in the blue hose.
4. Replace CleanJet pump.

title: Bus Signal Error
cause: Communication error between the PCB and the motor/ignition module.
fix:
1. Check the ribbon cable connections on the main PCB.
2. Inspect for moisture/corrosion on the board.
3. Replace the bus cable.

title: Care Pump Error
cause: The Care (descaling) pump is not running or is blocked.
fix:
1. Check the Care pump for blockages (scale chunks).
2. Verify the level electrode is clean.
3. Replace the Care pump.

title: Ignition Lockout
cause: The fryer failed to light after 3 attempts.
fix:
1. Turn the power switch OFF.
2. Check if the gas valve is ON.
3. Wait 30 seconds.
4. Turn power ON to reset ignition module.

title: Open Temp Probe
cause: The temperature sensor is reading an open circuit (broken wire).
fix:
1. Check the probe connection at the control board.
2. Measure resistance of the probe (should be ~1000 ohms at room temp).
3. If infinite ohms, replace the probe.

title: High Limit Tripped
cause: Oil temperature exceeded 450°F (232°C). Safety shutdown.
fix:
1. Allow oil to cool below 400°F.
2. Press the red reset button inside the cabinet (behind the door).
3. If it trips again immediately, replace the High Limit thermostat.

title: Long Freeze Cycle
cause: The ice maker took too long to make a batch of ice (over 35-45 mins).
fix:
1. Clean the condenser coil (dust/grease).
2. Check water inlet temperature (too hot?).
3. Check for low refrigerant charge (bubbles in sight glass).

title: Long Harvest Cycle
cause: Ice is not dropping from the evaporator plate quickly enough.
fix:
1. Check if the ice thickness probe is dirty.
2. Verify the curtain switch operation.
3. Check for scale buildup on the evaporator plate.

title: High Temperature Safety
cause: Discharge temperature exceeded 127°F.
fix:
1. Check for dirty condenser filter.
2. Verify condenser fan operation.
3. Reset by pressing the 'Reset' button on the control board.

title: Long Freeze Safety
cause: Freeze cycle exceeded timer settings (possible water leak or low charge).
fix:
1. Check inlet water valve for leaking.
2. Check float switch alignment.
3. Verify hot gas valve is not leaking by.

title: Blower Motor Failure
cause: The main convection blower is not spinning or the sensor is bad.
fix:
1. Check for obstructions in the fan.
2. Spin the fan manually (unplugged!) to check bearings.
3. Replace Blower Motor Controller.

title: Door Switch Error
cause: The door is registered as open during a cook cycle.
fix:
1. Adjust the door latch hinges.
2. Check the microswitches on the door mechanism.
3. Replace door switches.

title: EC Temp High
cause: Electrical Compartment (EC) is overheating (>158°F).
fix:
1. Clean the rear cooling fan filter.
2. Ensure the oven has 2-inch clearance in the back.
3. Check if the cooling fan is running.

title: Drain Valve Open
cause: Safety switch detects the drain valve is not fully closed.
fix:
1. Close the drain valve handle completely.
2. Check if the microswitch behind the valve is bent.
3. If valve is closed but error persists, replace the switch.

title: Temp Probe Error
cause: Temperature probe reading out of range (Short or Open).
fix:
1. Check probe wiring at the I-12 computer.
2. Ohms check: Should be ~1000 ohms at 70°F.
3. Replace probe if faulty.

title: Open Cabinet Sensor
cause: Cabinet air sensor is disconnected or failed.
fix:
1. Check sensor connection on the control board.
2. Replace the Cabinet Sensor (Blue Wire).

title: Short Cabinet Sensor
cause: Cabinet air sensor has shorted out.
fix:
1. Inspect sensor wire for pinched insulation.
2. Replace the Cabinet Sensor.

title: High Temp Alarm
cause: Cabinet temp is above safe limit (>40°F for 1 hour).
fix:
1. Check if door was left open.
2. Clean the condenser coil.
3. Check evaporator fan operation.

title: Auger Torque Error
cause: The slush is too thick/frozen, overloading the motor.
fix:
1. Turn machine OFF for 30 mins to thaw.
2. Adjust the thickness setting screw (counter-clockwise).
3. Check syrup-to-water ratio (too much water freezes hard).

title: Temperature Sensor Bad
cause: Tank temperature sensor reading is invalid.
fix:
1. Descale the tank (scale buildup on sensor).
2. Check sensor wire continuity.
3. Replace temp sensor.

title: High Pressure Cut Out
cause: Compressor discharge pressure too high (overheating).
fix:
1. Clean the air filter screens.
2. Ensure proper airflow clearance.
3. Reset the High Pressure switch manually.

title: Barrel Temp Sensor
cause: Freezing cylinder temperature probe failure.
fix:
1. Check probe wiring.
2. Replace the barrel sensor.
